original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-sheaf-condition-holds}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0] smooth,
\linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf, \linebreak[0] fpqc\}$.
The functor defined in (\ref{equation-quasi-coherent-presheaf})
satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to any $\tau$-covering
$\{T_i \to T\}_{i \in I}$ of any scheme $T$ over $S$.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module. Define a presheaf on schemes over $S$ by $T\xrightarrow gS\longmapsto\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$, with the natural pullback restrictions. For every $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf, and fpqc, this is a sheaf for $\tau$-coverings: whenever $\{T_i\to T\}$ is such a covering, the sequence
$$0\to\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)\to\prod_i\Gamma(T_i,g_i^*g^*\mathcal F)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\Gamma(T_i\times_TT_j,\mathcal F|_{T_i\times_TT_j})$$
is an equalizer.
stage_b_review_note: Retains fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth, syntomic and Zariski sheaf conditions for T↦Γ(T,g*F) for any quasi-coherent F over S. The added equalizer expresses matching sections on pairwise fibre products and correct pullbacks.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-gives-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_S$-module.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sheaf $\mathcal{F}^a$ is a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}$-module on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$, as defined in
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-site-local}.
\item If $\tau = Zariski$ or $\tau = \etale$, then the sheaf
$\mathcal{F}^a$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-module on
$S_{Zar}$ or $S_\etale$ as defined in
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-site-local}.
\end{enumerate}
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Then $\mathcal F^a$ is quasi-coherent as a module on the big ringed $\tau$-site, for every indicated $\tau$. For $\tau$ equal to Zariski or étale, $\mathcal F^a$ is likewise quasi-coherent on the respective small ringed site.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves qc nature of the associated site module F^a for five BIG topologies (Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf), and separately on small Zariski and small étale sites; no unsupported small fppf conclusion.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fully-faithful-associated}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
Each of the functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}^a$
of Definition \ref{definition-structure-sheaf}
$$
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S) \to \QCoh((\Sch/S)_\tau, \mathcal{O})
\quad\text{or}\quad
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S) \to \QCoh(S_\tau, \mathcal{O})
$$
is fully faithful.
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). For each indicated $\tau$, the association $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^a$ is fully faithful from $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)$ to quasi-coherent modules on the big $\tau$-site; it is also fully faithful for the small Zariski and étale sites. Explicitly, for quasi-coherent $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ the natural map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F^a,\mathcal G^a)$ is bijective on each eligible site.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves full faithfulness of QCoh(S)→QCoh(big τ site) for five τ and analogous small Zariski/étale functors, including bijection on Hom sets for all qc F,G.

hypotheses: F,G are quasi-coherent on S; tau eligible; small sites only Zariski and étale.
conclusions: Hom sets of quasi-coherent sheaves are preserved and reflected by the associated site sheaf functors.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}^a$
defines an equivalence of categories
$$
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh((\Sch/S)_\tau, \mathcal{O})
$$
between the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on $S$ and the category
of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules on the big $\tau$ site of $S$.
\item Let $\tau = Zariski$ or $\tau = \etale$.
The functor $\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}^a$
defines an equivalence of categories
$$
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)
\longrightarrow
\QCoh(S_\tau, \mathcal{O})
$$
between the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on $S$ and the category
of quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}$-modules on the small $\tau$ site of $S$.
\end{enumerate}
stage_a_standalone_statement_draft:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). For any $\tau$ in the five listed topologies, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^a$ is an equivalence of categories $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}((\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau,\mathcal O)$. In addition, for $\tau$ equal to Zariski or étale the same construction is an equivalence $\operatorname{QCoh}(S)\simeq\operatorname{QCoh}(S_\tau,\mathcal O)$. No analogous small-site assertion is made for smooth, syntomic or fppf topologies.
stage_b_review_note: Preserves equivalence QCoh(S)≃QCoh(big τ site) in five topologies and equivalence with small sites only for Zariski/étale. The draft correctly distinguishes these two claims and does not extend small-site assertion.
